questions.question: An athlete crosses a distance of 3600 m in 12 minutes. What is his speed (in km/h)?
questions.questionHtml: An athlete crosses a distance of 3600 m in 12 minutes. What is his speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance = 3600 m

Time = 12 minutes

Concept Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculation:

⇒ We know that 1 km = 1000 m

⇒ 3600 m = \(\frac{3600}{1000}=3.6km\)

⇒ 1 hour = 60 minutes

⇒ So, 12 minutes = \(\frac{12}{60}=0.2\) hrs

⇒ Speed of an athlete = \(\frac{3.6}{0.2}=18\) km/h

Hence, the speed of an athlete is 18 km/h.

questions.question: A truck runs 492 km on 36 Litter of diesel. How many kilometres can it run on 33 Litter of diesel?

On 1 Litre of diesel it runs = 492/36 km = 41/3 km

On 33 Litre of diesel it runs = (41/3) × 33 = 451 km

questions.solution: Difference in speed of Ram and Shyam = 90 – 72 = 18 km/h ⇒ 18 km/h = 18 × \(\frac{1000}{3600}\) = 5 m/sec

questions.question: A train is running at a speed of 99 km/h. If the train is 565 m long, then what will be the time (in seconds) taken by it to cross a 975 m long tunnel?
questions.questionHtml: A train is running at a speed of 99 km/h. If the train is 565 m long, then what will be the time (in seconds) taken by it to cross a 975 m long tunnel?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance to cross = 565 + 975 = 1540 m

Speed of the train = 99 km/h = 99 × 5/18 = 55/2 m/s

Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Speed = 1540 ÷ (55/2) = 56 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 56 seconds.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the train = 565 m

Length of the tunnel = 975 m

Speed of the train = 99 km/h

Formula Used:

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Tunnel

⇒ Total Distance = 565 + 975 = 1540 m

⇒ Speed of the train in m/s = 99 × 5/18

⇒ Speed = 11 × 5/2 = 55/2 m/s

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time = 1540 ÷ (55/2)

⇒ Time = (1540 × 2) ÷ 55

⇒ Time = 28 × 2 = 56 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 56 seconds.

Additional Information

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing an Object with Length

When a train crosses a platform, bridge, or tunnel, the total distance covered is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the object being crossed.

Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary man, pole, or tree, the total distance covered is equal to the length of the train alone.

Relative Speed

If two trains move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S1 + S2. If they move in the same direction, it is S1 − S2.

questions.question: Amit & Sumit start walking from same point in opposite directions at the speed of 6 km/h and 4 km/h, respectively. How far will they be from each other after 4 hours?
questions.questionHtml: Amit & Sumit start walking from same point in opposite directions at the speed of 6 km/h and 4 km/h, respectively. How far will they be from each other after 4 hours?
questions.solution:
Given:

Amit & Sumit start walking from the same point in opposite directions at the speed of 6 km/h and 4 km/h

Formula Used:

Relative speed(For opposite direction) = x + y

Speed = Distance/Time

Calculations:

As they are moving in the same direction,

⇒ Relative speed(For opposite direction) = x + y = 6 + 4 = 10 km/h

The total distance they moved in 4 hours

⇒ Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ Distance = Speed x Time = 10 x 4 = 40 km

⇒ Hence, They will be 40 km apart from each other.

Speed = Distance/Time

Let the length of the bridge be l

questions.question: Two cars X and Y start running towards each other from two places 216 km apart. The ratio of the speeds of X and Y is 5 ∶ 7 and the speed of X is 60 km/h. After how many minutes will X and Y meet each other?
questions.questionHtml: Two cars X and Y start running towards each other from two places 216 km apart. The ratio of the speeds of X and Y is 5 ∶ 7 and the speed of X is 60 km/h. After how many minutes will X and Y meet each other?
questions.solution:
Given:

X and Y start running towards each other from two places = 216 km

The ratio of X and Y = 5 : 7

The speed of X = 60 km/h

Formula used:

Time = Distance/Speed

1 hr = 60 min

Calculation:

Let the ratio of speed of X and Y be 5x and 7x respectively

According to the question

⇒ 5x = 60

⇒ x = 12

Then,

Speed of Y = 7x = (7 × 12) = 84 km/h

Now,

Time = [216/(60 + 84)]

⇒ (216/144)

⇒ 1.5 Hour = (1.5 × 60) min

⇒ 90 min

∴ Time taken to meet X and Y is 90

questions.question: A car covered 150 km in 5 hours. If it travels at one-third its usual speed, then how much more time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.questionHtml: A car covered 150 km in 5 hours. If it travels at one-third its usual speed, then how much more time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance covered by car = 150 km

Time taken by the car = 5 hours

Formula used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Speed of car = 150/5

⇒ Speed of car = 30 km/h

According to the question, if he travels at 1/3rd of its usual speed then

⇒ Speed = 30/3 km/h

⇒ Speed = 10 km/h

⇒ Time taken to travel 150 km at reduced speed = 150/10 hours

⇒ Time taken to travel 150 km at reduced speed = 15 hours

⇒ Increase in time = (15 – 5) hours

⇒ Increase in time 10 hours

∴ It will take 10 hours more to cover same distance if speed gets reduced to 1/3rd its usual speed. 
         Shortcut Trick
As per the question,

Speed ratio = 3:1

Time ratio = 1:3 

Given 1 unit = 5 hour so 3 unit = 15 hour  

Increase in time = (15 – 5) hours = 10 hours

questions.question: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a pole in 12 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take to cross a bridge 360 m long?
questions.questionHtml: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a pole in 12 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take to cross a bridge 360 m long?
questions.solution:

Speed = 72 km/h

Time = 12 sec

Distance = 360 m

Formula used:

Time = Distance/Speed

Calculation:

Speed = 72 × 5/18

⇒ 20 m/s

Distance = Length = (20 × 12) m

⇒ 240 m

Now,

Time = Distance/Speed

⇒ (360 + 240)/20

⇒ 600/20

⇒ 30 sec

∴ Required time is 30 sec

questions.question: A train travelling from Mumbai to Goa covered the first 420 km at a speed of 60 km/h and then covered the remaining 195 km at a speed of 65 km/h. Find its average speed in km/h.
questions.questionHtml: A train travelling from Mumbai to Goa covered the first 420 km at a speed of 60 km/h and then covered the remaining 195 km at a speed of 65 km/h. Find its average speed in km/h.
questions.solution:

Total distance is 420 + 195 = 615 km, Total time taken is 7 + 3 = 10 hr

So average speed is 615 /10 = 61.5 km/h

questions.question: Two trains A and B start running at 80km/h and 82 km/h towards each other from two different stations. They meet after 1 hour and 30 minutes. How far were they from each other when they started?
questions.questionHtml: Two trains A and B start running at 80km/h and 82 km/h towards each other from two different stations. They meet after 1 hour and 30 minutes. How far were they from each other when they started?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of train A = 82 km/h

Speed of train B = 80 km/h

They meet after 1 hour 30 min

Formula Used:

Relative Speed(In opposite direction) = x + y

Speed = Distance x Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = x + y = 82 + 80 = 162 km/h = 45 m/s

They meet after 1 hour 30 min

⇒ Time = 1 hour 30 min = 90 min = 90 x 60 = 5400 sec

Distance they covered 

⇒ Distance = Speed x Time = 45 x 5400 = 243000 m = 243 km

⇒ Hence, The distance between the two trains is 243 km.

questions.question: The speeds of A and B are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5. A takes 30 minutes more than B to reach the destination. In how much time does A reach the destination?
questions.questionHtml: The speeds of A and B are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5. A takes 30 minutes more than B to reach the destination. In how much time does A reach the destination?
questions.solution:
Given :

Ratio of speeds of A and B = 3 : 5

Calculation :

Ratio of speeds of A and B = 3 : 5

Hence, ratio of time taken by A and B will be = 5 : 3

∵ A takes 30 minutes more than B and the difference in Time taken by A and B = 5 - 3 = 2 Unit

i.e. 2 Unit = 30 Minutes

So , 1 Unit = 15 Minutes 

Time taken by A to reach the destination = 5 Unit

i.e. ( 5 × 15 ) minutes

⇒ 75 minutes = 75/60 hours = 1 hour 15 minutes 

Hence, the correct answer is "1 hour 15 minutes".

questions.question: A truck goes from Haryana to Bangalore with an average speed of 60 km/h. The journey takes 30 hours. It returns from Bangalore to Haryana on the same road with an average speed of 40 km/h. What was the average speed of the truck during the roundtrip?
questions.questionHtml: A truck goes from Haryana to Bangalore with an average speed of 60 km/h. The journey takes 30 hours. It returns from Bangalore to Haryana on the same road with an average speed of 40 km/h. What was the average speed of the truck during the roundtrip?
questions.solution:
Given:

A truck goes from Haryana to Bangalore with an average speed of 60 km/h

Time of the journey = 30 hours

Average speed from Bangalore to Haryana = 40 km/h 

Concept Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Average speed = \(\frac{Total\space Distance}{Total\space Time}\)

Calculation:

⇒ Ratio of speeds = 60:40

⇒ Ratio of time = 2:3

⇒ Time of the whole journey = 30 hours

⇒ Ratio of the time = 2:3

⇒ If 5 units is 30 hours

⇒ Then time periods are 12 hours and 18 hours

⇒ Distance From Haryana to Bangalore = 60 × 12 = 720 km

⇒ Whole journey = 2 × 720 = 1440 km

⇒ Average speed = \(\frac{1440}{30}\) = 48 km/h

Therefore, the average speed of the truck is 48 km/h

⇒ New speed = (6/7)S ,⇒ New time = (T + 20/60) hr

questions.question: Two trains 121 m and 99 m in length, respectively, are running in opposite directions, one at a speed of 40 km/h and the other at a speed of 32 km/h. In what time will they be completely clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.questionHtml: Two trains 121 m and 99 m in length, respectively, are running in opposite directions, one at a speed of 40 km/h and the other at a speed of 32 km/h. In what time will they be completely clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.solution:
Given:

Length of two trains are 121 m and 99 m running in opposite directions

Speed of 1st train is 40 km/h 

Speed of 2nd train is 32 km/h 

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time 

Calculation:

Here, we have total length of the train = (121 + 99) = 220 m 

As they are running in opposite directions having speeds of 40 km/h and 32 km/h respectively

So, their relative speed = (40 + 32) = 72 km/h = 72 × \(\frac{5}{18}\) = 20 m/s   [As 1 km/h = \(\frac{5}{18}\) m/s]

Now,

Time = \(\frac{Distance}{Speed}\)

⇒ Time = \(\frac{220}{20}\) = 11 seconds  

Hence,  the required time is 11 seconds.

⇒ Sum of their lengths = 200 m + 250 m = 450 m

⇒ Time = 450 / 5 = 90 seconds

A person covers 700 m distance in 6 minutes

Speed = Distance/time

Calculation:

Speed = v, Distance = 700 meter, time = 6 minutes

v = 700/6 (m/minute)

Here,

1 m = 1/1000 km

1 minute= 1/60 hour

⇒ v = (700/1000)/(6/60)

⇒ v = (700 × 60)/(6 × 1000)

⇒ v = 7km/hr

And speed change from km/hr to m/minute so multiply by 50/3

Here,

v = (700/6) × (3/50)

⇒ v = 70/10 km/hr

⇒ v = 7 km/hr

and initial time be t and new time be t1

⇒ s1 : s2 = 5 : 9

As the distance is constant the reverse of the ratio speed will give as ratio of time

⇒ t : t1 = 9 : 5

⇒ t - t1 = 40

⇒ 9x - 5x = 40 

⇒ 4x = 40 ⇒ x = 10

⇒ initial time = t = 9x = 9 × 10

∴ The usual time take by the boy to go school is 90mins

Alternate Method  

Let the normal time taken by him = X

as he increases his speed by 9/5 times the time taken decreases by 5/9 times

New time taken = 5/9X

⇒ X - 5/9X = 4/9X = 40 min

⇒ X = 90 mins

∴ The usual time taken by the boy to go to school is 90mins

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 kmph and including stoppages, it is 54 kmph. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
questions.questionHtml: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 kmph and including stoppages, it is 54 kmph. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
questions.solution: Stoppage per hour = [60 - 54]/60 × 60 min ⇒ 6 min

questions.question: In a race around a circular cycling track of 75 km, two cyclists are riding at a speed of 30 km/h and 25 km/h. After what time (in hours) will they meet at the point from where they started their journey?
questions.questionHtml: In a race around a circular cycling track of 75 km, two cyclists are riding at a speed of 30 km/h and 25 km/h. After what time (in hours) will they meet at the point from where they started their journey?
questions.solution:
LCM of fractions = [LCM of numerators of fractions] / [HCF of denominators of fractions]

Time taken by each to cover one round = 75/35

Time taken by each to cover one round = 75/25 

∴ Required time = LCM(75, 75) / HCF(35, 25) = 75/5  = 15 hours

questions.question: The distance covered by a train in (5y - 1) hours is (125y 3 - 1) km. The speed of the train is :
questions.questionHtml: The distance covered by a train in (5y - 1) hours is (125y<sup>3</sup> - 1) km. The speed of the train is :
questions.solution: Speed of the train ⇒ (125y3 - 1) ÷ (5y - 1) ⇒ \(\frac {(5y)^3 - 1}{(5y - 1)}\) ⇒ \(\frac {(5y - 1)(25y^2 + 5y + 1)}{(5y - 1)}\) ⇒ (25y2 + 5y + 1) km/h

questions.question: A car covers a particular distance in 3 hours with the speed of 54km/h. If the speed is increased by 27km/h, the time taken by the car to cover the same distance will be:
questions.questionHtml: A car covers a particular distance in 3 hours with the speed of 54km/h. If the speed is increased by 27km/h, the time taken by the car to cover the same distance will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

A car covers a particular distance in 3 hours with a speed of 54km/h.

The speed is increased by 27km/h

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/Time

Calculations:

According to the question,

Total distance travelled by car = 54 × 3 = 162 km

Total increased speed = 54 + 27 = 81 km/h

New Time required,

T = 162/81 = 2h

∴ The time taken by the car to cover the same distance will be 2 hours.

questions.question: A person reaches his destination 30 minutes late, if his speed is 3 km/h, and reaches 30 minutes before time if his speed is 4 km/h. Find the distance of his destination from his starting point.
questions.questionHtml: A person reaches his destination 30 minutes late, if his speed is 3 km/h, and reaches 30 minutes before time if his speed is 4 km/h. Find the distance of his destination from his starting point.
questions.solution:
Given:

The person is 30 minutes late when traveling at 3 km/h.

The person is 30 minutes early when traveling at 4 km/h.

Formula used:

Time taken at 3 km/h: T + 1/2 = D / 3

Time taken at 4 km/h: T - 1/2 = D / 4

Calculation:

From equation (1): T = (D / 3) - 1/2

From equation (2): T = (D / 4) + 1/2

Equating both: (D / 3) - 1/2 = (D / 4) + 1/2

⇒ (4D - 3D) / 12 = 1

⇒ D / 12 = 1

⇒ D = 12

∴ The distance to the destination is 12 km.

questions.question: A bus covers a 60-kilometre distance in 1 hour 15 minutes, whereas the same distance is covered by a car in 45 minutes. What is the ratio of the speed of the bus to the speed of the car?
questions.questionHtml: A bus covers a 60-kilometre distance in 1 hour 15 minutes, whereas the same distance is covered by a car in 45 minutes. What is the ratio of the speed of the bus to the speed of the car?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Time taken by the bus = 1 hr 15 min = 75 min

Time taken by the car = 45 min

Ratio of time taken (Bus : Car) = 75 : 45 = 5 : 3

Ratio of their speeds (Bus : Car) = 3 : 5

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance = 60 km

Time taken by bus (TB) = 1 hour 15 minutes = 75 minutes = 75/60 hours = 5/4 hours

Time taken by car (TC) = 45 minutes = 45/60 hours = 3/4 hours

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:

⇒ Speed of bus (SB) = 60 ÷ (5/4)

⇒ SB = 60 × (4/5) = 48 km/hr

⇒ Speed of car (SC) = 60 ÷ (3/4)

⇒ SC = 60 × (4/3) = 80 km/hr

⇒ Ratio of speed of bus to speed of car = SB : SC

⇒ Ratio = 48 : 80

⇒ Ratio = 3 : 5

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 5.

Additional Information

Proportionality in Speed, Time, and Distance

If distance is constant, Speed ∝ 1 / Time. If speed is constant, Distance ∝ Time. If time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If a body covers equal distances at speeds S1 and S2, then Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S1 − S2). In opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S1 + S2).

Relative speed is (45 - 27) × 5/18 = 5 m/s

Time will be, 1600/ 5 = 320 seconds

questions.question: A boat can travel 60km downstream in 4 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water is 13 km/h, then in what time will it cover 30 km upstream?
questions.questionHtml: A boat can travel 60km downstream in 4 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water is 13 km/h, then in what time will it cover 30 km upstream?
questions.solution:
Speed downstream = 60 km / 4 h = 15 km/h

Speed of stream = 15 km/h - 13 km/h = 2 km/h

Speed upstream = 13 km/h - 2 km/h = 11 km/h

Time upstream = 30 km / 11 km/h = 28/11 hours

questions.question: Kapila covers a distance of 1200 meters in 10 minutes. What is the speed of Kapila?
questions.questionHtml: Kapila covers a distance of 1200 meters in 10 minutes. What is the speed of Kapila?
questions.solution:
The speed of Kapila is 1200 meters/10 minutes = 120 meters/minute.

Converting 120 meters/minute to km/hr = 120 x (1/60) x (18/5) = 7.2 km/hr.

questions.question: Sahil covers a distance of 96 km at the speed of 16 km/h and covers another distance at the speed of 21 km/h in 5 hours. What is his average speed (in km/h)? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.questionHtml: Sahil covers a distance of 96 km at the speed of 16 km/h and covers another distance at the speed of 21 km/h in 5 hours. What is his average speed (in km/h)? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
Distance2 = Speed2 × Time2, Distance2 = 21 km/h × 5 h = 105 km

 

Total Distance = Distance1 + Distance2, Total Distance = 96 km + 105 km = 201 km

 

Time1 = Distance1 / Speed1, Time1 = 96 km / 16 km/h = 6 h

 

Total Time = Time1 + Time2, Total Time = 6 h + 5 h = 11 h


Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time, Average Speed = 201 km / 11 h ≈ 18.27 km/h

questions.question: Two men walk from a place at speeds of 9 km/h and 12 km/h, respectively. The first man takes 20 minutes more than the second one to cover the journey. Find the distance of the journey.
questions.questionHtml: Two men walk from a place at speeds of 9 km/h and 12 km/h, respectively. The first man takes 20 minutes more than the second one to cover the journey. Find the distance of the journey.
questions.solution: The distance is = [(9 × 12)/(12 - 9)] × 1/3 = 12 km

questions.question: Ravi can row a boat in still water at the speed of 14 km/h. If a river is flowing at the sped of 2 km/h and Ravi takes 3 hours to cover a certain distance upstream, then how much time will he take to cover the same distance downstream?
questions.questionHtml: Ravi can row a boat in still water at the speed of 14 km/h. If a river is flowing at the sped of 2 km/h and Ravi takes 3 hours to cover a certain distance upstream, then how much time will he take to cover the same distance downstream?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of the boat = 14kmph

Flow of the river = 2 kmph

Ravi takes 3 hours to cover a certain distance upstream

Concept used:

Distance = Time × Speed

While going upstream, the speed of a boat and the flow of the river get added to calculate the effective speed. On the other hand, while going downstream, to take the effective speed, the difference between the speed of the boat and the flow of the river is considered. 

Calculation:

Effective speed during the upstream journey = (14 - 2) kmph = 12kmph

Distance covered = 12 × 3 = 36 hours

Effective speed during the downstream journey = (14 + 2) kmph = 16kmph

So, time taken by Ravi to cover 36 km downstream = 36 ÷ 16 = 2.25 hours = 2 hours 15 minutes

∴ Ravi will take 2 hours 15 minutes to cover the same distance downstream.
